explanation: Copy every original row, then write each destination cell (r,c) from original cell (n-1-c,r). Reading from the snapshot prevents earlier writes from corrupting later source values, while cell assignment preserves the supplied matrix and its row objects.
timeComplexity: O(n squared): copying the n-by-n matrix and assigning all n squared destination cells each take one full pass.
spaceComplexity: O(n squared) auxiliary space for the independent row snapshot; loop indices use constant space.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Java algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A clockwise rotation sends an original cell (a,b) to (b,n-1-a). Solving for the source of destination (r,c) gives (n-1-c,r), exactly the copied value assigned by the loops. Every destination is written once from the unchanged snapshot, so no original value is lost.
walkthrough: For [[2,5],[7,9]], the snapshot remains unchanged while destination row 0 reads original (1,0)=7 and (0,0)=2. Destination row 1 reads original (1,1)=9 and (0,1)=5. The supplied matrix becomes [[7,2],[9,5]]. The method returns no value; the wrapper displays that mutated matrix. The callable returns no value; expected records the original matrix after mutation, and the harness additionally checks row identity.
edgeCases: The input matrix must be square.
The original row objects must be preserved.
